ECMAScript 2026 Language Specification — TOC digest (extract)
This document defines the ECMAScript language. It is organized into
numbered clauses.

1 Scope
2 Conformance
3 Normative references
4 Overview
  4.1 Web Scripting
  4.2 Hosts and Implementations
  4.3 ECMAScript Overview
  4.4 Terms and Definitions
5 Notational Conventions
  5.1 Syntactic and Lexical Grammars
  5.2 Types and values
6 ECMAScript Data Types and Values
  6.1 ECMAScript Language Types
  6.2 ECMAScript Specification Types
7 Abstract Operations
  7.1 Type Conversion
  7.2 Testing and Comparison Operations
  7.3 Operations on Objects
8 Executable Code and Execution Contexts
  8.1 Lexical Environments
  8.2 Code Evaluation
9 Ordinary and Exotic Objects Behaviours
  9.1 Proxy Object Internal Methods
  9.3 ECMAScript Function Objects
10 The Global Object, Functions and Constructors
  10.1 Global Object
  10.2 Function Objects
  10.3 Built-in Function Objects
11 ECMAScript Language: Source Text
  11.1 Source Text
  11.4 Comments
  11.6 Names and Keywords
12 ECMAScript Language: Lexical Grammar
  12.1 Unicode Format-Control Characters
  12.9 Keywords and Reserved Words
  12.10 Punctuators
13 ECMAScript Language: Expressions
  13.2 Primary Expression
  13.3 Left-Hand-Side Expressions
  13.11 Conditional Operator
  13.12 Assignment Operators
  13.14 Binary Bitwise Operators
  13.15 Exponentiation Operator
  13.16 Binary Logical Operators
14 ECMAScript Language: Statements and Declarations
  14.1 Statement Semantics
  14.6 Iteration Statements
  14.7 The try Statement
  14.8 The throw Statement
  14.9 The return Statement
15 ECMAScript Language: Functions and Classes
  15.1 Parameter Lists
  15.2 Function Definitions
  15.4 Class Definitions
  15.6 Generators
  15.7 Async Functions and Async Generators
16 ECMAScript Language: Scripts and Modules
  16.1 Scripts
  16.2 Modules
  16.3 ImportDeclaration
  16.4 ExportDeclaration
17 ECMAScript Language: Memory Model
18 ECMAScript Language: Arrays and Objects
19 Control Abstraction Objects
  19.2 Promise Objects
  19.3 Generator and Async Function Objects
20 Numbers and Dates
  20.1 Number Objects
  20.2 BigInt Objects
  20.4 Date Objects
21 Text Processing
  21.2 String Objects
  21.3 RegExp (Regular Expression) Objects
22 Indexed Collections
  22.1 Array Objects
  22.2 TypedArray Objects
23 Keyed Collections
  23.1 Map Objects
  23.2 Set Objects
24 Structured Data
  24.1 ArrayBuffer Objects
  24.2 SharedArrayBuffer Objects
  24.3 DataView Objects
25 Control Abstractions Objects (4th edition
  25.1 Promise Jobs and Capability Records
  25.2 AsyncFunction Objects
26 Reflection
  26.1 Proxy Objects
  26.2 Module Namespace Objects
27 Memory and Garbage Collection
28 Objects: Builtin
  28.1 Function Properties of the Global Object
  28.2 Value Properties of the Global Object
  29 The Shared Memory and Atomics
Key sections: 9 Ordinary and Exotic Objects Behaviours; 13 Expressions;
14 Statements; 15 Functions and Classes; 17 Memory Model; 21 Text
Processing; 22 Indexed Collections; 23 Keyed Collections; 26 Reflection.
The full specification is several thousand pages; agents should consult
the official ECMA-262 document for normative text, and this digest for
structure and terminology.
